from.place: the second equality in the pre-derived adjunction calculation: representing a localized morphism by a right fraction

title: Every localized morphism has a right-fraction representative
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $S$ a class of its arrows with a right calculus of fractions [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], and $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a localization at $S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For objects $M,N$ and every morphism $g:Q(M)\to Q(N)$, there are an object $P$, an arrow $s:P\to M$ in $S$, and an arrow $f:P\to N$ such that $g=Q(f)\circ Q(s)^{-1}$.
